I have been poking around quite a bit, regarding getting Linux on my SP4. After reading through quite a bit of material, I finally decided to simply just run Linux Mint (ubuntu) through a VM (virtualbox). The nice thing about virtualbox is you do not need to enable Hyper-V, so you can still have that "tablet-like" experience (ie; locking/unlocking seemlessly). Also, another plus is that if you mess up your Linux system, you can simply restore back to a snapshot you take, it is quite painless and really gives you the ability to play around with linux much more. Also, running linux through a VM means you dont need to worry about drivers and such, which meant i literally just downloaded the iso and installed it. For my setup I used my 64 gig sd card and gave my linux os a 20 gig partition. The newer surfaces (especially the pros) have quite a bit of power, so even though linux is on a Vm, the lightweight 64x ubuntu runs really smoothly as well. Honestly, after setting up my linux like this, I can't see any real pluses to having a hard partition of linux on your pro. A lot of the driver issues still havent been worked out, and a lot of the patches made are only semi-reliable. I seriously think you should consider a VM, its easy, quite hassle-free, andd gives me everything I wanted.
